title: Energy in reactions - 123 school
heading: Energy in reactions
intro: These questions are about exothermic and endothermic reactions, heat of reaction, heat of formation and activation energy.
Test your knowledge by typing your answer and comparing it with the correct answer. Then click 'Check answers'.

questions.q: What is an exothermic reaction?
questions.a: A reaction in which energy (heat) is released; the surroundings get warmer

questions.q: What is an endothermic reaction?
questions.a: A reaction in which energy is absorbed; the surroundings get colder

questions.q: Which sign does the heat of reaction have for an exothermic reaction in BINAS?
questions.a: Negative (–), because the energy content of the substances decreases

questions.q: Which sign does the heat of reaction have for an endothermic reaction?
In which unit is the heat of reaction given in BINAS?
questions.a: In J per mole (in tables 56 and 57 in 10<sup>5</sup> J/mol)

questions.q: What is the heat of formation of a substance?
questions.a: The energy released or absorbed when 1 mole of the substance is formed from the elements (at 298 K and p<sub>0</sub>)

questions.q: What is the heat of formation of an element in its standard state, for example O<sub>2</sub>(g)?
questions.a: 0 J/mol (so elements are not listed in BINAS table 57)

questions.q: In which BINAS table do you find heats of formation of inorganic substances?
How do you calculate the heat of reaction from heats of formation?
questions.a: Heat of reaction = sum of the heats of formation of the products – sum of the heats of formation of the starting substances (take the coefficients into account)

questions.a: (–3.935 + 2 × (–2.86)) – (–0.75) = –8.905·10<sup>5</sup> J; this agrees with the heat of combustion of methane in table 56

questions.q: What is activation energy?
questions.a: The minimum energy that molecules must have in a collision to react

questions.q: Why does a mixture of methane and oxygen not react by itself at room temperature, although the reaction is exothermic?
questions.a: The activation energy is too high; a spark or flame is needed first to start the reaction

questions.q: What does a catalyst do to the activation energy and to the heat of reaction?
questions.a: The activation energy becomes lower; the heat of reaction stays the same

questions.q: Why is a reaction faster at a higher temperature?
questions.a: More collisions have enough energy to reach the activation energy (and there are more collisions per second)

questions.q: In an energy diagram the products lie lower than the starting substances. Is the reaction exothermic or endothermic?
What do you read from an energy diagram as the difference between the top of the curve and the level of the starting substances?
What takes energy: breaking bonds or forming bonds?
questions.a: Breaking bonds takes energy; forming bonds releases energy

questions.q: In a reaction the energy needed to break bonds is smaller than the energy released when new bonds form. Is the reaction exothermic or endothermic?
Give an example of an endothermic reaction from daily life
questions.a: For example photosynthesis, or dissolving ammonium nitrate in a cold pack

questions.q: Give an example of an exothermic reaction from daily life
questions.a: For example the combustion of natural gas, or iron rusting in a hand warmer
